cases.name: Kaladaa Crowell
cases.about:
She was a case worker at the Jerome Golden Center for Behavioral Health, a mental-health facility in West Palm Beach. She had worked at the center almost as long as she lived in the area and helped clients re-enter society, said Dr. Suresh Rajpara, the center’s chief medical officer. Heidi Harris said Crowell became a “second mom” to her patients. Before Christmas, she took clients to get free haircuts. She spent six weeks teaching Creole to those interested at the center. At the end of the class, in November, she even convinced a Haitian restaurant to cater a party she threw for her students. Kaladaa decorated her home and place of employment for every holiday. She loved holidays and had started a business last year to sell gift baskets and to plan parties. “She celebrated every birthday and holiday as if it was her last,” her sister said.

cases.name: Kyra Kalis Inglett
cases.about:
She was a fifth-grade student at Northboro Elementary School, greeted neighbors as she rode her purple bicycle and was known for known for her “spunky” demeanor and artistic talents. She took voice lessons, danced and was a talented artist. Kyra worked for 20 volunteer hours to earn a bike from the local nonprofit Jack the Bike Man, Harris said. Jack Hairston, who runs the nonprofit, said Kyra worked hard in his shop during the summer as part of the eight-session “Gotta Get A Bike” program to learn how to disassemble and reassemble the purple bike that she later took home.
